pr_title: Fix Sonos cover art when browsing albums
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR fixes two bugs:

1. When the album art URI is prepared for proxy, the backslash separating album name from query type was not properly encoded, resulting in a requests for which the hass didn't have a registered view because MediaPlayerview does not allow backslashes in the ID. This was causing 404s for all of the albums.

2. After addressing the initial 404 I have noticed that only some of the covers were loading correctly. Investigation revealed that they are also matched in very inefficient way - that is by finding all tracks of a given album, then matching album based on that. In other words, for each album, Sonos was queried for all the tracks that the album may have, then album art uri was retrieved. The SoCo library allows for more direct queries, where we only retrieve the specific album. This has improved speed a lot and fixed all of the missing covers.

issue_context.title: Covert Art missing when browsing Sonos Media Library
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I am using Sonos media player that is configured to play media from attached NAS. The files are shared through CIFS. When browsing the list of albums, there is no cover art displayed. Just a lot of empty boxes that waste a lot of space.

Steps to reproduce:
1. on a Media player card, click "Browse media"
2. Select "Music Library" (with the Sonos icon)
3. Select "Albums"
4. Observe that list of empty boxes is loaded:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/183976/178116581-dbb2b82e-22f7-46e5-bf54-1d539a272c3e.png)

After inspecting the boxes with devtools they have a `background` set to seemingly correct address, however each of those requests results in 404 Not Found response. The example url would be:

```
url(/api/media_player_proxy/media_player.living_room/browse_media/album/A:ALBUM/If%20You%20Wait?token=6e26b324a8177fd22a1586999ece88490f85e4da588e7e2fe42db1b9c29b2b4a&authSig=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..UtneZDIUf9ef5-onO0dR80yOjOA0lZWrM45Q8iIsFFM)
```

Visiting that through browser also results in 404 Not found and absolutely nothing in the log files (I'm running full debug).

Please note that album art for the same album (and all others) works correctly when the media is actually played. However, at that point the image is already cached and the URL above would be ```https://hass.example.com/api/media_player_proxy/media_player.living_room?token=717fd9720e52d00dc9cd026a0af7518d21b12c274d85f6c8d4cfce262317431d&cache=3037394ef4418fee```

I was trying to trace back the code to see how the cache gets populated and it correctly points to the Sonos' URL that presumably is received from SoCo as `album_art_uri`. That example URI was

`http://192.168.1.121:1400/getaa?u=x-file-cifs%3a%2f%2fapollo.home%2fdownloaded_music%2fLondon%2520Grammar%2520-%2520Wasting%2520My%2520Young%2520Years%2520%255bEP%255d%2520(2013)%2520%255bFLAC%255d%2f01%2520-%2520Wasting%2520My%2520Young%2520Years.flac&v=16``

and it displays covert art correctly. So looks like the bug is somewhere that is supposed to handle the `media_player_proxy` call for  the albums, but I was not able to find where.




### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.8.0.dev20220704

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

sonos

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

comments:
Hey there @cgtobi, @jjlawren, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`sonos`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L986) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I have figured out why it is broken and returning 404 responses. When the `MediaPlayerImageView` component [registers the external proxy URLs](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6a376009364935af7524751c8bff10097a0ce3e2/homeassistant/components/media_player/__init__.py#L1086), the expected format is `base_url + "/browse_media/{media_content_type}/{media_content_id}",` while the Sonos extension adds an extra part (`/A:ALBUM`) like for example

`/browse_media/album/A:ALBUM/If%20You%20Wait`

The extra chunk makes `aiohttp` not match on that URL at all.

If I get some spare time, I'll try to work on fix unless someone beats me to it
